concepts.def: Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
Withholding information or misleading participants; permitted only if no alternative and harm is minimal.
Participants must be free to leave at any point without penalty, including withdrawing their data.
Participants must be protected from physical and psychological harm beyond everyday experience.
Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.
British Psychological Society Code of Ethics and Conduct sets four principles: respect, competence, responsibility, integrity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Issues and Debates in Psychology — a core area of A-Level Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Issues and Debates in Psychology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Issues and Debates in Psychology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many principles does the BPS Code of Ethics contain?
If deception is used, what must be provided afterwards?
options: Debrief
Reward
Public apology
Withdrawal fee
Removing an unpleasant stimulus to INCREASE a behaviour.
Punishing a behaviour to decrease it.
Giving a reward to decrease behaviour.
Picking participants who match the population profile.
Picking participants who match the population profile.
Every member of the target population has an equal chance of selection.
Just grabbing whoever is around (any haphazard method).
Giving a reward to decrease behaviour.

mcqs.q: Why does the cognitive approach use INFERENCE?
options: Mental processes cannot be directly observed, so they are inferred from behaviour.
Because brain scans are unreliable.
Because cognitive psychologists guess instead of measuring.
Giving a reward to decrease behaviour.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Informed consent”?
options: Participants must be free to leave at any point without penalty, including withdrawing their data.
Full explanation after the study including its true aim and opportunity for participants to ask questions.
Withholding information or misleading participants; permitted only if no alternative and harm is minimal.
Participants must understand the study and agree to take part; presumptive consent used if deception is unavoidable.
